text:
Nashville is 13-6-6, 7-2-1 in its last ten, and sitting on 32 points with a 64% playoff chance by our simulations. The question is how much of it will hold, and the honest answer is: some. They have 49.9% of the expected goals (the quality of chances on both sides), dead even, and their points total runs about five ahead of what those chances earned. Juuse Saros and the goaltending have saved about eight goals more than expected, and that is the cushion.

Friday showed both sides of it. The Predators scored five on 2.26 expected goals against Utah, led with four minutes left, and lost in a shootout to a team that out-attempted them 78-48. Being outplayed at five on five (47% of the expected goals) is the pattern to watch.

The best line has been the young one: Filip Forsberg with Nils Hoglander and Shane Wright, 55% of the expected goals and an 11-4 goal edge. The Steven Stamkos and Ryan O'Reilly line sits at 44%, and O'Reilly's name came up in the Wild's centre search after they missed on Dylan Larkin. Roman Josi and Adam Wilsby drive play, but have been outscored 19-14 together. Watch whether Saros can keep covering the gap.
